cl_benzo_liking.q: Do benzos get you high, and who actually likes them?
cl_benzo_liking.short: Depends who you are. In one lab study, 27 of 36 people without drug problems mostly chose a dummy pill over Valium. People with past drug problems almost always chose benzos.
cl_benzo_liking.but: But those people were tested in other labs' studies, mostly with much bigger doses. So we can't tell if their past made the difference.
how: In a 1980s study, 36 young volunteers with no history of drug problems (most had tried cannabis) tried Valium and a dummy pill, then chose between them five times. Most picked the dummy pill, anxious or not.
Valium calmed them and made them sleepy and a bit muddled. It didn't raise their scores for euphoria. At the higher dose they felt more tired and less cheerful than on the dummy pill.

A review of older lab studies found that people with a history of drug problems almost always chose benzos. Moderate drinkers chose Valium more than light drinkers did. Anxious people chose benzos when they could take them as needed.

Outside the lab, some people say they get high. In an older US school survey, about half of teens who took calming pills without a prescription said they usually got high. In a newer adult survey, 12 in 100 who misused benzos said getting high was their main reason.
cl_benzo_liking.rate: Small, old lab studies. The one read in full was careful, but the comparison between kinds of people comes second-hand from a review of separate studies that used very different doses.

cl_benzo_misuse_reasons.q: Why do people misuse Xanax and other benzos?
cl_benzo_misuse_reasons.short: Mostly to relax or sleep, they say. In a big US survey, 47 in 100 people who misused benzos named relaxing as the main reason, 27 sleep, and 12 getting high.
cl_benzo_misuse_reasons.but: It's what people told a survey. And 'misuse' here also counts taking more of your own pills than your doctor said.
how: In a US survey in 2015 and 2016, about 13 in 100 adults had used a benzo in the past year. About 2 in 100 had misused one. At ages 18 to 25, about half of all benzo use was misuse.
Misuse meant any use a doctor didn't direct. Most often (74 in 100) it was pills without a prescription. Three in four had misused alprazolam (Xanax).
Main reasons: relaxing 47 in 100, sleep 27, getting high 12, coping with feelings 10. These add up to a bit over 100, and the paper doesn't say why.
About 69 in 100 got the pills from a friend or relative, mostly for free, and 20 in 100 from one doctor. About 7 in 100 met the criteria for dependence.
cl_benzo_misuse_reasons.rate: One big national survey of US adults, chosen to stand for the whole country. But it's people's own answers, nobody checked them, and people in institutions such as prisons, or in the military, weren't asked.

benzodiazepines.statement: Most people would pick Valium over a dummy pill.
benzodiazepines.why: In a lab study, most young volunteers without drug problems chose the dummy pill. It was one small study, and people with a history of drug problems did choose benzos in other studies.

benzodiazepines.statement: People with anxiety liked Valium more than others in a lab test.
benzodiazepines.why: In one small study, anxious volunteers neither chose nor liked it more, though it eased their anxiety. Studies that let anxious people take it as needed did find a preference.

benzodiazepines.statement: Most people who misuse benzos say they do it to get high.
benzodiazepines.why: In a big US survey, 12 in 100 named getting high as their main reason. Relaxing (47 in 100) and sleep (27) came first, by people's own account.

general.statement: Most people who misuse benzos are hooked on them.
general.why: In a big US survey, about 7 in 100 people who misused benzos met the criteria for dependence. 'Misuse' there includes taking your own pills more often than prescribed.
